64gb_2x32.note: Cheapest: PNY Performance $799.95 (Walmart marketplace); cheapest name-brand: Crucial $1,002.57 (Newegg)

fleet_economics: At these prices a 16->64 GB DDR4 upgrade (~$300-430 used) costs 1.5-2x a sub-$199 fleet node itself. Dominant play: buy nodes with RAM already installed; the RAM in the deal can be worth more than the box. See tools/dealsdesk/mini_node_scorer.py.
market_context: Gartner (2026-04-08): DRAM +125% in 2026, no meaningful relief until late 2027. Micron is exiting the Crucial consumer brand (shipments through Feb 2026, warranty continues).
scope_note: SO-DIMM (laptop / mini-PC) memory only. Server RDIMM (DDR3 Gen8 strategy, DDR4 Gen9) is a different market and is NOT covered by these numbers.
sources: Live listings checked 2026-10-20 across Newegg, Walmart, Best Buy and eBay. Used figures are active Buy It Now asks plus live auctions; eBay completed-sale prices sit behind sign-in and were not verified. Amazon is excluded (refuses AI-agent access).

valuation_for_scorers.note: Installed-RAM values use used-market midpoints (the fleet buys used) and are nonlinear: 32 GB sticks carry a premium. Upgradeability factor = historical_norm_gb_price / current gb_price, clamped 0..1 — as RAM gets more expensive, empty slots are worth less (Brian's rule, 2026-10-20).
